courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computer Science Principles
courses.description: Capabilities and applications of computers. Algorithmic problem-solving methods and computer programming. Using computers to examine questions from other fields of study. Practical and theoretical limits to computation. Machine intelligence and heuristic problem solving. Social and legal impact of computers.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introductory Computer Programming
courses.description: Computing methodology, process, and computational problem solving. Algorithm Design; program design, development, and testing. Formerly numbered as CS 107. Not open to students with credit in CS 107.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introductory Computer Programming Laboratory
courses.description: Programming experiences designed to demonstrate and reinforce concepts through active experimentation and programming exercises.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Intermediate Computer Programming
courses.description: Advanced computing methodology, process, and computational problem solving. Programming environment and data structures. Object-oriented program design and development. Binary trees, linear lists, maps, queues, recursion, stacks. Formerly numbered as CS 108

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Intermediate Computer Programming Laboratory
courses.description: Programming experiences designed to demonstrate and reinforce concepts through active experimentation and programming exercises.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science and Python
courses.description: Basic data analysis with Python to include confidence intervals, regression, and sampling. Data structures, displaying data, and programming constructs.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Data Structures
courses.description: Representations and operations on basic data structures. Arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, and recursion; binary search trees and balanced trees; hash tables, dynamic storage management; introduction to graphs. An object oriented programming language will be used. Formerly numbered as CS 310.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computer Organization
courses.description: Organization and assembly language to include CPU, logic circuits, and memory. Data representation, interrupts, looping and addressing techniques, macros, and traps. Formerly numbered as CS 237.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introduction to Software Systems
courses.description: Alternatives analyses, information management, networking and communications, parallel and distributed processing, principles and practices, security and encryption. Ethical, legal, and social issues in computing. Modeling will be used to capture and explore designs.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Logic gates, combinational circuits, sequential circuits, memory and bus system, control unit, CPU, exception processing, traps and interrupts, input-output and communication, reduced instruction set computers, use of simulators for analysis and design of computer circuits, and traps/interrupts.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Advanced Programming Languages
courses.description: Concurrent programming, logic programming, object-oriented programming. Implementation issues. Formerly numbered as CS 520.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: First-order logic. Heuristic and uninformed search. Deep neural networks, hierarchical clustering, k-means, linear regression, support vector machines. Image classification and object tracking. Language models, parsing, speech generation. Formerly numbered as CS 550.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Algorithms
courses.description: Algorithms for solving frequently occurring problems. Analysis techniques, divide and conquer algorithms with applications, graph problems, greedy algorithms. Introduction to NP complete problems. Formerly numbered as CS 560.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: UNIX System Administration
courses.description: Installing the UNIX operating system on a UNIX workstation, adding user accounts, backing up and restoring user files, installing windows, adding network capabilities, adding printers and other peripherals.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Operating Systems
courses.description: File system, I/O management, interprocess communication, memory management, processes and threads, program structures, thread synchronization, virtual memory. Formerly numbered as CS 570.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Senior Capstone Project 2
courses.description: Second course in a two-semester sequence where students form teams and build software systems to address real-world needs. Teams use modern design techniques to analyze, specify, design, and prototype solutions.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Undergraduate Honors Thesis
courses.description: Directed reseach in computer science and completion of honors thesis. Thesis to be presented at the annual SDSU Research Symposium and/or defended before a committee of faculty. Maximum credit six units.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Special Study
courses.description: Individual study. Maximum credit six units.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Database Theory and Implementation
courses.description: Database systems architecture. Storage structures and access techniques. Relational model, relational algebra and calculus, normalization of relations, hierarchical and network models. Current database systems. Not open to students with credit in CS 503

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Systems Programming
courses.description: Design and implementation of system software. Relationship between software design and machine architecture. Assemblers, compilers, debuggers, editors, linkers and loaders, macro processors. Object oriented concepts and programming fundamentals. Not acceptable for the M.S. degree in computer science.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Machine Learning
courses.description: Algorithms and computer methods for machine learning. Supervised methods: convolutional neural networks, feedforward neural networks, linear regression, logistic regression, support vector machine; unsupervised methods: dimensionality reduction, k-means clustering, subspace learning. Applications in classification, regression and visualization.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Robotics
courses.description: Robotic systems and their components. Spatial descriptions and transformations. Kinematics and inverse kinematics of robots. Robotic programming and simulation environments to include Matlab Robotics Toolbox. Mobile robots. Trajectory tracking and control. Path planning.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Approaches on deep neural networks. Common tasks, modern programming frameworks, and state-of-the-art models.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computer Networks and Distributed Systems
courses.description: Basic networking concepts to include seven-layer reference model, transmission media, addressing, subnetting and supernetting, networking devices, LANs and WANs, internetworking, distributed processing, and client-server model. Basic concepts and protocols of TCP/IP protocol suite and basic Internet services.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Principles and Techniques of Data Science
courses.description: Data classification, cleaning, common representation and operations, dimensionality reduction, hypothesis testing, life cycle, regression, statistical inference, and visualization.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Wireless Networks
courses.description: Current and future protocols, fundamental theories, low power Internet of things and wireless sensor networks.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computational Linguistics
courses.description: Basic concepts in computational linguistics including finite-state transducers, n-gram language models, vector space semantics, statistical classifiers, neural nets, and transformers. Applications to parsing, natural language understanding, and large language models.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introduction to Speech Processing
courses.description: Fundamentals of speech processing and speech recognition. Physical aspects of speech production and perception. Mathematical models for speech recognition. Corpus development: data collection, processing, and evaluation. Applications of speech processing and associated research topics.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: 3D Game Programming
courses.description: Development of programming skills using software environment of a game engine and its scripting language. 3D concepts for game play, modeling, and programming. Roles needed in software development team. Contrast creation of original 3D object models for game world with incorporation of pre-created generic models.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Advanced 3D Game Programming: Multi-Player Games, Simulations, and Virtual Worlds
courses.description: Advanced concepts and techniques of multiplayer multiplatform video game programming. Artificial intelligence techniques for designing intellgent behaviors and creating lifelike behaviors in characters to provide realism and lifelike opponents. Virtual and augmented reality.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Scientific Computing
courses.description: Parallel programming using message passing to include high performance computing and MPI language extensions.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computational Genomics and Bioinformatics
courses.description: Biological and genomics data. Application of computational algorithms to biological questions. Post-genomic techniques in annotation and comparison of microbial and eukaryotic genome sequences.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Big Data Tools and Methods
courses.description: Analyze, curate, search, and visualize big data. Apache MapReduce and Spark, distributed databases and messaging/streaming, electronic notebooks, NoSQL databases, programming languages, statistics.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Machine Learning Operations
courses.description: MLOps life cycle, data versioning, reproducibility, continuous integration and delivery for ML pipelines, monitoring and model drift detection, scalability, ethical considerations, model retraining, model evaluation, automation, hands-on experience with modern MLOps tools and frameworks.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Foundations of Deep Learning
courses.description: Foundations of deep learning systems and how they adapt to real-world applications. DL Optimization, DL Generalization, Neural Tangent Kernels, Robustness for DL, Deep Generative Models, Self-supervised DL, Transformers, Domain adaptation and generalization, Explainable DL, and Meta-Learning. Project-oriented implementing advanced algorithms.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Visual Perception and Learning
courses.description: Computer algorithms and methods for computer vision. Edge detection, histogram of gradients, image filtering, machine learning, robust matching and model fitting, scale-invariant feature transform, stereo vision and 3D scene reconstruction. Object detection, recognition, and visual tracking.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Algorithm Analysis and Design
courses.description: Algorithm design techniques. Approximation algorithms and reductions among NP-complete problems. Greedy and divide and conquer algorithms. Linear and dynamic programming. Graph algorithms and network flow. NP and computational interactability.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Algorithms for Big Data
courses.description: This course covers the design and analysis of algorithms and machine learning in computational models that capture the computation of massive data such as streaming, sublinear, and parallel models.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Applied Large Language Models
courses.description: Large Language Models (LLM), understanding how an LLM works, training and refining LLMs, preparing data to train an LLM, testing and debugging LLMs, hardening LLMs against attacks, prompt engineering.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Practicum in Teaching of Computer Science
courses.description: Supervision in teaching computer science. Lecture writing, style of lecture presentation and alternatives, test and syllabus construction, and grading system. Not applicable to an advanced degree. Required for first semester GTA's.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Curricular Practical Training
courses.description: Supervised work experience. Maximum credit three units applicable to a master?s degree in computer science.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Research
courses.description: Research in computer science. Maximum credit six units applicable to a master's degree.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Special Study
courses.description: Individual study. Maximum credit six units applicable to a master's degree.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Thesis or Project
courses.description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master's degree.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Thesis or Project Extension
courses.description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
courses.description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master's degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
